newsitem.title: USA: Wittnauer watches sold by Westinghouse.
newsitem.headline: Wittnauer watches sold by Westinghouse.

text.p: Wittnauer International Inc. said senior management had completed a management buyout of the 116-year-old watchmaker from Westinghouse Electric Co.

The buyout of Wittnauer comes less than a month after former Saudi oil minister Sheikh Ahmed Zaki Yamani sold Vacheron Constantin, the world's oldest maker of high quality watches, to Vendome Luxury Group Plc of Britain. Terms were not disclosed but industry sources estimated the price at about $80 million.
Reynald Swift, president of Wittnauer International, led the management team in the buyout from Westinghouse.
The company was founded in 1880 by Albert Wittnauer, a Swiss who became a marketer of fine watches and timepieces. Westinghouse acquired the firm in 1969.

In addition to making and selling a full range of Wittnauer watches, Wittnauer distributes the Universal Geneve brand and the 114-year-old Zodiac line of sports watches. Earlier this year, it began distributing Adidas and Ellesse watches. In Canada, Wittnauer also distributes the Baume & Mercier watch line.
